*I’d block the merge on two findings.*

1. *[P1] Validation accepts a valid substring, not the whole slug* — `src/validate.js:1–4`  
   `/[a-z0-9-]+/` matches anywhere in the input. I confirmed `Ahello`, `hello/world`, `hello.world`, `hello world`, and `"hello\n"` all pass and produce URLs through `pagePath`. Encoding invalid characters doesn’t enforce the documented slug rules.  
   *Recommendation:* require the entire nonempty string to contain only allowed characters. Include trailing-newline tests—JavaScript’s `$` anchor alone can accept a final line terminator.

2. *[P1] Reserved slugs aren’t enforced by the public path builder* — `src/route.js:3–5`  
   `isReserved` exists but is never called by validation or `pagePath`. I confirmed `pagePath('admin')` returns `/p/admin`; `new`, `edit`, and `api` also pass. This defeats the reservation intended to prevent collisions with app routes.  
   *Recommendation:* reject reserved names in the path-building flow and test all four through `pagePath`, not just the standalone helper.

All four existing tests pass, but they miss both failures. Reviewed `slug-validation` at `e8612a7` against `main` at `9ba0eca`. No code changed.
